query: How can melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties be determined accurately and efficiently across the high-entropy-alloy family? State the physical rationale, expected quantitative performance, range of applicability, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive validation result that would rule out the proposed approach.

generation.hypothesis: Calphad-based computational thermodynamics can accurately predict the melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
generation.intervention: Calphad-based computational thermodynamics with key parameters: alloy composition, temperature range, and thermodynamic database
generation.conditions: Alloy composition: 3-6 principal elements, Temperature range: 298-2000 K
generation.predicted_outcome: Mean absolute error in melting temperature: < 50 K, Mean absolute error in enthalpy of fusion: < 10 J/g, Mean absolute error in entropy of fusion: < 0.1 J/gK
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in thermodynamic database, Uncertainty in alloy composition

falsification_experiment.design: Compute melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties for a set of high-entropy alloys using Calphad-based computational thermodynamics and compare with experimental measurements
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the mean absolute error in melting temperature exceeds 100 K or the mean absolute error in enthalpy of fusion exceeds 20 J/g for more than 20% of the alloys, the hypothesis is falsified
